lead: McKinney plumbing deals with clay soil, a historic downtown and fast-growing subdivisions. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across McKinney.
risk: slab leaks in clay soil, aging pipes in historic homes and burst pipes in hard freezes
risk_short: slab leaks, old pipes and frozen pipes
why: Historic Downtown McKinney has homes from the late 1800s and early 1900s with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron or clay drains. Most of the city, like Stonebridge Ranch and Craig Ranch, was built after 1990 on slabs.
Expansive clay moves with drought and heavy rain, which stresses lines under slabs. Rare hard freezes burst attic and exterior-wall pipes.
utility: City of McKinney Water (from the North Texas Municipal Water District)
water: McKinney buys treated water from the North Texas Municipal Water District, which draws largely from Lavon Lake. The water is moderately hard.
tips: Water your foundation evenly in dry summers.
Scope old sewer lines before buying a historic home.
Get irrigation backflow devices tested when required.
areas: PipeMend works in Historic Downtown, Craig Ranch, Stonebridge Ranch, Tucker Hill, Trinity Falls, Eldorado, Adriatica and every other McKinney neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of McKinney Building Inspections Department, and plumbers must hold a Texas license.

faq.q: Do historic McKinney homes need repiping?
faq.a: Many do. Homes built before the 1950s often have galvanized steel supply pipes that rust inside, lowering pressure and causing leaks. PEX or copper repiping fixes both.
